subject: Certificate assertion choreography for private FQDNs — Greenlight Bank POC
messages:
From: Evan Turner <evan.turner@greenlightbank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@greenlightbank.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Certificate assertion choreography for private FQDNs — Greenlight Bank POC

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're starting the network design for the private deployment POC and need to lock down how certificates and TLS will be handled for our internal-only FQDNs (examples: api.greenlight.internal, worker.greenlight.internal). A few specific questions: 

- Do you recommend Redwood terminate TLS at the customer VPC endpoint (Redwood private endpoint) or should we use a pure passthrough so we can present client certs to backends?
- If Redwood terminates, what footprint do you need from our PKI (SANs, intermediate CA, OCSP responders)?
- For mutual TLS, can Redwood validate client certs against our internal CA, or do we need to upload client certs to Redwood?

I've attached a rough topology diagram to show the network layout (greenlight_poc_topology.pdf). We're mindful of audit requirements (we need certificate fingerprint logs for every handshake) and of certificate rotation windows. Ideally we can get a short checklist and recommended Cipher suites/CSPs so our infosec can sign off.

Can we aim to finalize approach by next Wednesday (2027-04-06)?

Thanks,
Evan Turner
Sr. Platform Engineer
Greenlight Bank

Attachment: greenlight_poc_topology.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Turner <evan.turner@greenlightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Certificate assertion choreography for private FQDNs — Greenlight Bank POC

Hi Evan / Maya,

Appreciate the topology — that helps a lot. High level there are three common patterns we recommend for private deployments; I'll list the tradeoffs and what we need from Greenlight PKI for each. I've attached a short matrix (cert_assertion_matrix.xlsx) that maps compliance asks to each option.

1) Redwood-terminated TLS at the private endpoint
   - Pros: simpler from backend perspective, Redwood can handle OCSP stapling and renewals, easier to centralize observability (fingerprint logging on our side).
   - Cons: requires you to provide leaf certificates (or a delegated CA) for SANs we will serve; we need documented trust chain and ACLs for which SANs are customer-owned.
   - What we need: leaf certs (PEM), intermediate cert chain, list of FQDNs, OCSP responder URL if you require stapling from your CA, rotation window policy.

2) Passthrough / mTLS to customer backends (recommended if you must preserve client identity)
   - Pros: end-to-end client cert visibility, Greenlight controls auth.
   - Cons: more complex routing, requires SRV/port mapping and health checks; Redwood will act as TCP/L4 forwarder for TLS (we can optionally inspect SNI to route).
   - What we need: your CA bundle for validation, sample client certs for testing, explicit list of allowed client CA fingerprints for initial allowlist.

3) Hybrid (TLS terminated but with client cert assertion headers)
   - Pros: gives backend an asserted client identity without full passthrough.
   - Cons: requires mutual agreement on how assertions are signed and transported (we support signed JWT assertion headers).
   - What we need: an assertion signing key exchange + public key, HMAC secret or RSA pubkey, and allowed header names.

Given your audit constraint (certificate fingerprint logs), option 1 or 3 gives the cleanest server-side logging path. If you must keep raw client certs at the backend for internal auth, option 2 is the safer route.

Quick follow-ups:
- Can you confirm whether Greenlight policy allows uploading intermediate certs to a hosted vendor?
- Who is the PKI owner on your side for CSR/signing?

I'll loop Karthik for a detailed checklist and sample CSR fields.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: cert_assertion_matrix.xlsx
From: Evan Turner <evan.turner@greenlightbank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@greenlightbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Certificate assertion choreography for private FQDNs — Greenlight Bank POC

Grace — thanks, that breakdown is helpful. Our compliance and app teams discussed this morning and we lean toward option 2 (mTLS passthrough) for the POC because several auth checks in our platform validate presented client certs end-to-end. A few notes and asks: 

- We cannot upload intermediate/private keys to a third party; providing CA bundles for validation is OK.
- We need an explicit checklist for the certificate exchange (which files to pull, fingerprint expectations, rotation notice windows).
- Audit requirement: Redwood must emit a per-handshake event with client_cert_fingerprint and server_cert_fingerprint to a dedicated logging endpoint (we can provide a collector).

I'll get the PKI owner (Maya) to share the canonical CA bundle and a set of test client certs. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports TLS passthrough with SNI-based routing to multiple backends? Also can you give us a recommended initial cipher suite list (we prefer modern TLS1.3-only if possible)?

Thanks — Evan

Attachment: greenlight_poc_requirements.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Turner <evan.turner@greenlightbank.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Certificate assertion choreography for private FQDNs — Greenlight Bank POC

Evan / Maya / Grace,

Thanks for the direction, Evan. Below is a pragmatic checklist and configuration playbook for option 2 (mTLS passthrough) tailored to the POC. I've included sample fields and the minimum audit outputs Redwood will emit.

Checklist (action items and artifacts):
- Greenlight provides:
  • CA bundle (PEM, full chain) — filename: greenlight_ca_bundle.pem
  • A set of 3 test client certs (PEM) and corresponding private keys (for test harness only) — test_client_1.pem/.key etc.
  • List of private FQDNs and SNI mappings (CSV)
  • Collector endpoint for audit events (HTTPS endpoint + auth token)

- Redwood will provide:
  • Ingress listener configuration that performs TCP passthrough for port 443 and SNI-based routing to tenant backends.
  • Validation layer that verifies client cert chains against provided GH CA bundle (we will not require you to upload private keys).
  • Per-handshake audit event with fields: timestamp, client_cert_fingerprint (SHA256 hex), server_cert_fingerprint (SHA256 hex), sni, src_ip (masked as required), backend_target, handshake_result. These events are POSTed to your collector endpoint and retained per contract.
  • Recommended TLS policy: TLS1.3 only; cipher suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384; key exchange X25519/P-256 for interoperability.
  • OCSP/CRL: for passthrough we will validate certs against CA bundle; we can optionally consult your OCSP responder if you provide reachable URL and SLA for responses.

Rotation and revocation plan:
- Certificate rotation window: Greenlight signals rotations 14 days in advance to Redwood.
- For revocation events, Greenlight must notify Redwood on IR channel and provide certificate serial numbers; Redwood will block matching fingerprints immediately and confirm via audit.

CSR/sample for Greenwood leaf certs (for the rare case of Redwood-generated leaf certs; not required for pure passthrough):
- CN: <fqdn> (e.g., api.greenlight.internal)
- SAN: DNS:<fqdn>, IP:optional
- O: Greenlight Bank, OU: Platform, C:US

Operational notes:
- Health checks: we will perform L4 health checks to the backend TLS listener; ensure backend responds to a TCP probe on configured port.
- SNI routing caveat: if you use identical SNI for multiple backends we need per-path rules; please provide explicit mapping.
- Fingerprint format: SHA256 hex (lowercase) — sample: 3a:4f:... (we will provide hash utilities).

Next steps:
1) Maya — please upload CA bundle and one test client cert to the shared drive link (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-ExampleDriveLink) and ping me when done.
2) Grace / Ben — I'll open INF-4721 in Jira to track the config work and share the playbook artifacts (csr_templates.tar.gz and cert-exchange-playbook.md attached).
3) Let's schedule a 45-min runbook review next week to validate end-to-end.

If anything here conflicts with Greenlight policy let us know and we'll adapt — otherwise we'll queue the infra work after we see the CA bundle.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

Attachments: csr_templates.tar.gz, cert-exchange-playbook.md
